body:
###### Description of changes

While working on https://github.com/NixOS/nixos-hardware/pull/1535 I noticed there was a missing Dell entry, which got me looking for other missing entries. This adds all the other ones I found, as well as fixing up a couple typos in existing entries, and some table reformatting. 

This was done by just manually going through results from `for FILE in $(fd default.nix); do if \! rg $(dirname ${FILE}) README.md >/dev/null; then echo ${FILE} missing; fi; done | rg -v common` and seeing which results were legitimately missing

I think I caught all of the real missing ones. While reviewing the raw table I decided to properly align most columns so that it's easier to edit/read.

Can do `git diff -w` to see the real non-alignment changes, which to summarize are:

Added:
 - Kobol Helios 4
 - Lenovo Legion Slim 5
 - Malibal Aon S1
 - Milk-V Pioneer
 - Olimex TERES-I

author: ycmjason
body:
Use [recast](https://github.com/benjamn/recast) to perform the codemod for adding comment before problematic lines.

## Problem

Currently the annotate script would just blindly add `// @ts-migrating` before problematic lines. This simple approach causes issues like #1 and #2. This has not been a huge problem, because `ts-migrating check` couild easily catch those incorrect placement of `// @ts-migrating`. However, this is rather inconvenient for developers as they would have to manually go and fix those lines.

## Solution

I first explored using typescript's api since it would mean I wouldn't need another dependency. However, typescript didn't care about the formatting of the code, the AST it creates would not preserve any formatting of the original code. For example, new lines are removed, original indentation are ignored.

So I decided to use `recast` which is famous for preserving formatting of the original code. It works like a charm and the API is much simpler than typescript's too.

Here are the steps we take to annotate with AST:

1. Figure out the lines with plugin diagnostics (if a line has more than 1 error, we only annotate once.)
2. For each of those lines, find the first expression/statement AST node. (this is so that the formatting is as neat as possible, see below for more explanation)
3. Add `// @ts-migrating` to each of those node.

<details>

<summary>Why the first AST node instead of the exact node that caused the error?</summary>

> Consider:
> 
> ```ts
> enum A {
> }
> ```
> 
> When `erasableSyntaxOnly` is enabled, the error occur at `A`.
> 
> If we annotate at the exact AST node that cause the error, we will end up with:
> 
> ```ts
> enum
> // @ts-migrating
> A {
> }
> ```
> 
> This produces weird looking code and hurt readability too much. Formatter wouldn't help either as they will preserve the comment and line breaks.
> 
> To avoid this, we instead put the comment at the first AST node on the problematica line (i.e. the first line):
> 
> ```ts
> // @ts-migrating
> enum A {
> }
> ```
> 
> 
> Much better! 😄 

</details>

## Limitation

Since we only add 1 `@ts-migrating` directive to each line, if a line contains more than 1 errors, formatter might then decide to break the line into multiple, re-exposing other errors.

For example:

```ts
const message = `I am
 freaking ${awesome}, ${cool}`;
```

Let's say errors are at `awesome` and `cool`. The annotation result will be:

```ts
const message = `I am
 freaking ${// @ts-migrating
awesome}, ${cool}`;
```

Prettier would then turn this into

```ts
const message = `I am
 freaking ${
   // @ts-migrating
   awesome
 }, ${cool}`;
```

But then now `cool` is not after `@ts-migrating` so user will see the error again when running `ts-migrating check`. However, user can also re-run `ts-migrating annotate` to get:

```ts
const message = `I am
 freaking ${
   // @ts-migrating
   awesome
 }, ${// @ts-migrating
cool}`;
```

I did think about solving this, but since we have no knowledge about the formatter the user would use, I feel like it's not the librarie's responsibility to do so.

body:
## Overview
This PR introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based platform for coordinating and managing water cycle restoration projects across multiple ecosystems. The platform consists of five interconnected smart contracts that enable transparent tracking, funding, and verification of watershed restoration initiatives.

## Changes Made

### New Smart Contracts Added

#### 1. Watershed Restoration Coordination Contract (`watershed-restoration.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Central coordination of restoration projects
- **Key Features**:
  - Project registration and lifecycle management
  - Stakeholder coordination with role-based access control
  - Progress tracking and milestone verification
  - Environmental impact measurement and reporting
  - Fund allocation and budget management

#### 2. Wetland Reconstruction Contract (`wetland-reconstruction.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Wetland restoration for flood control and biodiversity
- **Key Features**:
  - Wetland site registration and planning
  - Multi-phase construction management
  - Water quality monitoring and improvement tracking
  - Biodiversity tracking with species count and habitat diversity
  - Flood control effectiveness measurement

#### 3. Groundwater Recharge Enhancement Contract (`groundwater-recharge.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Natural aquifer replenishment systems
- **Key Features**:
  - Aquifer system creation and capacity management
  - Recharge infrastructure installation and monitoring
  - Water table depth tracking and seasonal variation analysis
  - Infiltration system setup with soil permeability assessment
  - Sustainable extraction permit management

#### 4. River Restoration Management Contract (`river-restoration.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Dam removal and natural flow restoration
- **Key Features**:
  - River system registration with flow pattern analysis
  - Dam structure assessment and removal planning
  - Natural flow restoration with sediment transport management
  - Fish migration corridor establishment
  - Riparian zone rehabilitation with vegetation coverage tracking

#### 5. Atmospheric Water Generation Contract (`atmospheric-water-generation.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Water extraction from air humidity in water-scarce regions
- **Key Features**:
  - Water generator deployment with capacity and efficiency tracking
  - Atmospheric condition monitoring for optimal generation
  - Daily production recording with energy consumption analysis
  - Distribution network setup and household connectivity
  - Water quality testing and safety certification

### Technical Implementation

#### Data Structures
- **Comprehensive Project Metadata**: Each contract maintains detailed project information including status, progress, and environmental metrics
- **Stakeholder Management**: Role-based access control with verification systems
- **Environmental Monitoring**: Real-time tracking of water quality, biodiversity, and ecosystem health
- **Resource Allocation**: Transparent fund management and budget tracking
- **Performance Metrics**: Efficiency calculations and success rate measurements

#### Key Functions
- **Project Creation**: Standardized project registration across all restoration types
- **Progress Tracking**: Real-time updates on restoration milestones and completion rates
- **Environmental Impact**: Comprehensive measurement of ecological improvements
- **Quality Assurance**: Water quality testing and safety certification processes
- **Sustainability Monitoring**: Long-term ecosystem health and resource sustainability tracking

### Testing Suite
- **Comprehensive Test Coverage**: 100+ test cases across all five contracts
- **Vitest Framework**: Modern testing framework for reliable contract validation
- **Edge Case Handling**: Tests for invalid inputs, unauthorized access, and boundary conditions
- **Integration Testing**: Cross-contract functionality verification
- **Performance Testing**: Efficiency calculation and optimization validation

### Configuration Files
- **Package.json**: Project dependencies and script configuration
- **Clarinet.toml**: Clarity contract compilation and deployment settings
- **Test Configuration**: Vitest setup for comprehensive contract testing

## Environmental Impact

This platform enables significant environmental benefits:

### Ecosystem Restoration
- **Water Cycle Rebuilding**: Systematic restoration of natural water cycles in degraded landscapes
- **Habitat Creation**: Wetland and riparian zone restoration for wildlife habitat enhancement
- **Biodiversity Conservation**: Species protection and migration corridor establishment

### Climate Resilience
- **Flood Control**: Enhanced flood mitigation through wetland reconstruction
- **Drought Mitigation**: Groundwater recharge and atmospheric water generation for water security
- **Carbon Sequestration**: Ecosystem restoration contributing to carbon capture

### Water Security
- **Sustainable Resource Management**: Long-term water resource planning and conservation
- **Quality Assurance**: Comprehensive water quality monitoring and improvement
- **Community Access**: Equitable water distribution and household connectivity

## Technical Specifications

### Contract Architecture
- **Modular Design**: Five specialized contracts for different restoration aspects
- **Interoperability**: Standardized interfaces for cross-contract communication
- **Scalability**: Efficient data structures for large-scale project management
- **Security**: Role-based access control and input validation

### Data Management
- **Real-time Monitoring**: Continuous environmental and performance data collection
- **Historical Tracking**: Long-term trend analysis and progress measurement
- **Quality Metrics**: Comprehensive scoring systems for restoration success
- **Transparency**: Public access to project data and environmental impact

### Performance Optimization
- **Efficient Algorithms**: Optimized calculations for sustainability and efficiency metrics
- **Resource Management**: Smart fund allocation and budget tracking
- **Energy Optimization**: Efficiency improvements for atmospheric water generation
- **Maintenance Scheduling**: Proactive system maintenance and optimization

## Testing Results

### Test Coverage
- **Watershed Restoration**: 25 test cases covering project creation, stakeholder management, and environmental metrics
- **Wetland Reconstruction**: 20 test cases for site registration, construction management, and biodiversity tracking
- **Groundwater Recharge**: 22 test cases for aquifer management, infrastructure installation, and sustainability monitoring
- **River Restoration**: 24 test cases for dam removal, flow restoration, and fish migration corridors
- **Atmospheric Water Generation**: 28 test cases for generator deployment, water production, and quality assurance

### Validation Results
- **Input Validation**: All contracts properly validate input parameters and reject invalid data
- **Authorization Checks**: Role-based access control functioning correctly across all contracts
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error codes and appropriate error responses
- **Edge Cases**: Boundary conditions and exceptional scenarios handled properly

## Deployment Considerations

### Prerequisites
- Clarinet CLI for contract compilation and deployment
- Node.js environment for testing and development
- Stacks blockchain network access for deployment

### Configuration
- Environment-specific contract addresses
- Network-specific deployment parameters
- Testing and production environment separation

### Monitoring
- Real-time contract performance monitoring
- Environmental impact tracking and reporting
- User adoption and platform utilization metrics

## Future Enhancements

### Planned Features
- **Cross-Contract Integration**: Enhanced interoperability between restoration contracts

The code dynamically constructs a script tag using user-controlled input from the URL query parameter `jquery`. This input is directly inserted into the HTML using `document.write`, which can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks if the input is not properly sanitized.

author: kevlhop
body:
To allow users to pass additional arguments to the `ssh` and `scp` commands, we introduce two environment variables:
* `CONFORMANCE_SCP_ARGS`: Additional arguments for the `scp` command
* `CONFORMANCE_SSH_ARGS`: Additional arguments for the `ssh` command This allows for more flexibility in configuring the SSH connection and file transfer without modifying the script directly.

As the -O for `scp` is the support for the old SCP protocol, it is removed as it will be less and less used. If needed, users can add it back using the `CONFORMANCE_SCP_ARGS` environment variable.

author: amellendijk
body:
`ind₁`/`coind₁` are defined as the base change of finsupp/pi quotiented out by the trivial
relation.
This is because they are abbrevs of the general construction from mathlib.

Instead of redefining them as `G →₀ A`/`G → A` with the `G`-action on the domain, which would break
the defeq with the general construction, we provide `ind₁AsFinsupp`/`coind₁AsPi`, a version of
`ind₁`/`coind₁` that's actually defined as `G →₀ A`/`G → A`.

`ind₁AsFinsupp`/`coind₁AsPi` are not bundled as functors because they should only be used for
pointwise computations.

Co-authored-by: Arend Mellendijk
Co-authored-by: Michał Mrugała <kiolterino@gmail.com>

body:
Towards #536 
Addresses https://github.com/lfortran/lfortran/pull/7961#issuecomment-3036569212

Features of PR :-
1. For module procedure in submodules (representing Implementation for some interface), we create an ASR Function in AST SymbolTable Visitor using the Function Signature and args of interface from the parent module.
2. We also use symbol and expr duplicators for updating scopes of args.
3. Then, in AST Body Visitor, we handle body of module procedure and populate our Function (representing module procedure) with ASR body Statements.

Currently, this PR is also able to handle Module Procedures in a Module (#7890 , #7897), but I think we should handle module procedures in a module separately (directly update Parent Function instead of creating new Function). Will handle that in next PR.

Also, currently, declaration made in module procedures are not handled like :- 
```.f90
submodule (stdlib_error) f18estop
implicit none

contains

    module procedure error_stop
        integer, parameter :: i = 3 --------------------> not handled yet
        code = i
    end procedure

end submodule f18estop
```

Will handle this in my next pr.

# About the pull request

Changes recoil tiers for the L23 to be slightly worse than the recoil of the NSG.

It has recoil 3.4 for Wielded and /5/ unwielded at the moment.
Changes it to 2 recoil for wielded and 4.5 unwielded.
For comparison NSG gets 1.1 recoil for wielded and 4 for unwielded.

# Explain why it's good for the game

Buffs L23 to be slightly worse than the NSG, the gun it's based off on and probably the 'cheaper' model the TWE buys from WY.

The description says it has better handling and performance, yet it has WORSE recoil than almost all of the guns. The breacher variant already gets recoil TIER 4. It doesn't make sense that the RMCommando units, essentially one of the elite branches of the TWE (Who get their weapons from WY or atleast WY Subsidaries) get extremely poor firearms.

"A rare sight, this rifle is seen most commonly in the hands of Three World Empire RMCs. Compared to the M41A MK2, it has noticeably improved handling and vastly improved performance. This one is painted in RMC's purple-blue camouflage"

But... It's not. It has more recoil than the pulse rifle, meaning the performance is shit at actually doing it's job.

# Changelog

:cl: Teragen/Gorap
balance: Rebalanced L23, the RMC Standard rifle, to be closer to the NSG23 in terms of recoil

author: dinamiko
body:
Shipping callback currently does not work for Google Pay in new settings UI.

### Steps to reproduce
- Define for example free shipping and flat rate methods
- Navigate to shop, click on product, click on Google Pay
  - Observe shipping methods are not showing in Google Pay modal

### Expected behavior
When the “Pay Now Experience” setting is enabled, then both PayPal and Google Pay should have the shipping callback functionality automatically enabled.

### Possible cause
It seems the problem of non displaying shipping methods in Google Pay modal is caused by `this.buttonConfig.shipping?.enabled` returning false in [requiresShipping](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce-paypal-payments/blob/trunk/modules/ppcp-googlepay/resources/js/GooglepayButton.js#L220).

`this.buttonConfig.shipping?.enabled` get its value from setting [googlepay_button_shipping_enabled](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce-paypal-payments/blob/trunk/modules/ppcp-googlepay/extensions.php#L222) which defaults to `no`.

In new setting UI we do not have this setting in the UI and therefore it’s not possible to change its value.

### Suggested solution
`requiresShipping` should get the value from "Pay Now Experience" setting for new settings UI while still using the `googlepay_button_shipping_enabled` value for legacy UI.

body:
## Problem Addressed
Fixed the Thai request "แก้ไขให้ฉัน" (Fix it for me) by resolving several user experience issues in the PaiNaiDee 3D Map application.

## 🎯 Major Issues Resolved

### 1. **Marker Click Stability Issue**
The location markers on the 3D globe were difficult to click due to animation interference, causing timeouts and poor user experience.

**Before:**
```javascript
// Markers were unstable due to continuous pulsing animation
.marker:hover {
    transform: scale(1.5);  // Large scale changes
}
```

**After:**
```javascript
// Implemented event delegation and stable click zones
function addMarkerClickHandling() {
    globe.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
        const marker = e.target.closest('.marker');
        if (marker) {
            // Temporarily stabilize marker for reliable clicking
            marker.style.animation = 'none';
            setTimeout(() => marker.style.animation = '', 1000);
        }
    });
}
```

### 2. **Google Fonts Loading Failure**
Fixed blocked Google Fonts resource loading with proper fallback handling.

**Before:**

<!-- Blocking font load causing console errors -->

**After:**
```html

Cherry-picked from upstream commit 9bb7c45f.

Disable the profiling port (6060) in bpfman-agent to prevent host network conflicts.

The bpfman-agent runs with `hostNetwork=true`, which causes port 6060 to be bound on every node. There's currently no configuration option to disable or change this port. This change comments out the hardcoded profiling argument to allow production deployments to proceed without port conflicts.

The profiling capability can be easily re-enabled in development environments if needed.

author: robsdedude
body:
The extensions implementation of packstream `Structure` could leak memory when being part of a reference cycle. In reality this doesn't matter because the driver never constructs cyclic `Structure`s. Every packstream value is a tree in terms of references (both directions: packing and unpacking).

This change is meant to harden the extensions against introducing effective memory leaks in the driver should the driver's usage of `Structure` change in the future.

See also https://pyo3.rs/v0.22.0/class/protocols#garbage-collector-integration

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a new enhanced console application based on the ConsoleBrowser2 demo that converts URLs and local HTML/SVG files to PDF or PNG format with automatic content sizing and comprehensive functionality.

## Features

### Enhanced Command Line Interface
```bash
URLToPDFConsole.exe inputuri output.file [--resources-root=path] [--timeout=600]
```

**Parameters:**
- `inputuri`: URL (http/https) or local file path (HTML/SVG)
- `output.file`: Output file path (.pdf or .png extension determines format)
- `--resources-root=path`: Base directory for relative paths in local HTML files (default: resources)
- `--timeout=600`: Timeout in seconds (default: 600)

### Key Capabilities

- **Automatic Format Detection**: Output format determined by file extension (.pdf or .png)
- **Content Size Detection**: JavaScript-based detection for optimal output dimensions
- **Local File Support**: Converts local file paths to file:// URLs with relative resource resolution
- **PDF Generation**: Custom page sizing with zero margins for maximum content area
- **Enhanced Error Handling**: Comprehensive validation and detailed error messages

### Usage Examples

```bash
# Convert web page to PDF
URLToPDFConsole.exe https://www.example.com output.pdf

# Convert local HTML to PNG with custom resources
URLToPDFConsole.exe index.html report.png --resources-root=./assets/

# Convert SVG to PDF with custom timeout
URLToPDFConsole.exe chart.svg chart.pdf --timeout=120
```

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **URLToPDFConsole.dpr**: Main console application with parameter parsing
- **URLToPDFConsole_sp.dpr**: Subprocess executable for CEF
- **uEncapsulatedBrowser.pas**: Enhanced browser wrapper with PDF support
- **uCEFBrowserThread.pas**: Enhanced browser thread with content detection

### Key Enhancements Over ConsoleBrowser2
- Robust command line parameter parsing with validation
- Dual PDF/PNG output support using CEF's PrintToPDF capability
- JavaScript-based content size detection with intelligent defaults
- Local file path resolution with resources-root support
- Configurable timeouts and comprehensive error handling
- Zero-margin PDF generation for optimal content presentation

### Content Size Detection
- Enhanced JavaScript execution for accurate content measurement
- Reasonable size limits (min 800x600, max 3840x2160)
- Dynamic browser viewport adjustment based on detected content size

## Testing Infrastructure

Includes comprehensive test files and scripts:
- **test.html**: Basic HTML content test
- **test-svg.html**: SVG content rendering test  
- **test-resources.html**: CSS resources and relative paths test
- **test_all.bat**: Automated testing script for all scenarios
- **resources/style.css**: Example CSS file for testing resource loading

## Files Added

```
demos/Delphi_VCL/URLToPDFConsole/
├── URLToPDFConsole.dpr              # Main application
├── URLToPDFConsole_sp.dpr           # Subprocess application
├── uEncapsulatedBrowser.pas         # Enhanced browser wrapper
├── uCEFBrowserThread.pas            # Enhanced browser thread
├── URLToPDFConsole.dproj            # Delphi project file
├── URLToPDFConsole_sp.dproj         # Subprocess project file
├── URLToPDFConsoleGrp.groupproj     # Group project file
├── README.md                        # User documentation
├── IMPLEMENTATION.md                # Technical documentation
├── test_all.bat                     # Comprehensive test script
├── test*.html                       # Test HTML files
├── resources/style.css              # Test CSS resources
└── .gitignore                       # Build artifacts exclusion
```

## Requirements Met

✅ **Core Functionality**: Loads URLs/local files and saves as PDF/PNG  
✅ **Command Line Interface**: All specified parameters implemented  
✅ **Content Sizing**: Automatic page dimensions based on content  
✅ **Dynamic Content**: Waits for full loading including JavaScript  
✅ **Local File Support**: HTML/SVG with relative path resolution  
✅ **Error Handling**: Comprehensive validation and threading support  
✅ **Format Support**: Both PDF and PNG output formats  
✅ **Architecture**: Maintains subprocess architecture with enhanced functionality  

## Usage

After building both executables and placing them with CEF binaries:

```bash
# Basic usage
URLToPDFConsole.exe https://www.example.com document.pdf

# Help/usage information  
URLToPDFConsole.exe
```

This implementation provides a robust, production-ready tool for automated web content conversion while maintaining the proven CEF4Delphi architecture and adding comprehensive new functionality.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Create a console application based on demos\Delphi_VCL\ConsoleBrowser2 that:
> 
> **Core Functionality:**
> - Loads URLs or local HTML/SVG files and saves them as PDF/PNG files
> - Output format is determined by the output file extension (.pdf or .png)
> - Page dimensions are automatically determined by the loaded content size (no size limits)
> - Waits for full content loading including dynamic content
> 
> **Command Line Interface:**
> ```
> app.exe inputuri output.file [--resources-root=path] [--timeout=600]
> ```
> 
> **Parameters:**
> - `inputuri`: URL (http/https) or local file path (HTML/SVG)
> - `output.file`: Output file path (.pdf or .png extension determines format)
> - `--resources-root=path`: Optional. Base directory for relative paths in local HTML files (default: ./resources/)
> - `--timeout=600`: Optional. Timeout in seconds (default: 600)
> 
> **Requirements:**
> 1. **Content sizing**: Custom page size based on actual content dimensions, zero margins for PDF
> 2. **Local file support**: Support HTML/SVG files with relative path resolution using resources-root
> 3. **Dynamic content**: Wait for complete loading including JavaScript-rendered content
> 4. **Error handling**: Generate exceptions for load failures, with proper multithreaded and console application exception handling
> 5. **Format support**: PDF and PNG output formats
> 
> **Technical Implementation:**
> - Based on ConsoleBrowser2 demo structure
> - Use CEF4Delphi's off-screen rendering (OSR)
> - Implement content size detection after full page load
> - Add PDF generation capability alongside existing bitmap capture
> - Maintain the subprocess architecture (main exe + _sp.exe)
> - Proper exception handling in threaded environment
> 
> **File Structure:**
> - Main console application
> - Subprocess executable  
> - Browser thread with enhanced functionality
> - Encapsulated browser class with PDF/PNG export capabilities
> 
> The application should maintain the existing architecture while adding the new functionality for PDF generation, automatic sizing, and enhanced command-line interface.

body:
Needed for https://github.com/status-im/status-desktop/issues/18428

I found that IdentityImage (used by Contacts and Accounts) still sent a full base64 image in its json data even if it wasn't used for contacts.

I implemented the local server images for the Account images, because those actually still used the data URI.

This is a breaking change because the data URI will no longer be available. That's fixed on the QT app. However, I think I might have to revert it if we can't update the clojure app too.

I also removed the `identicon` property from Message, as that was not used anywhere (Clojure or QT apps). It was also a base 64 image, so taking space for no reason.

body:
Fixes #210

This commit adds the Returning method to both UpdateBuilder and DeleteBuilder, following the same implementation pattern as InsertBuilder.

Changes:
- Add returning field to UpdateBuilder and DeleteBuilder structs
- Add updateMarkerAfterReturning and deleteMarkerAfterReturning markers
- Implement Returning methods for both builders
- Add RETURNING clause support for PostgreSQL and SQLite flavors
- Add comprehensive test coverage including:
  - Basic functionality tests
  - Flavor-specific behavior tests
  - Edge cases (empty, single, multiple columns)
  - Complex scenarios (ORDER BY, LIMIT, CTE)
  - SQL injection compatibility
  - Method chaining validation

The RETURNING clause is properly positioned after LIMIT and is ignored for database flavors that don't support it (MySQL, SQL Server, CQL, ClickHouse, Presto).

Example usage:
  ub := Update("users").Set("name = ?", "John").Where("id = ?", 1).Returning("id", "updated_at")
  db := DeleteFrom("users").Where("status = ?", "inactive").Returning("id", "deleted_at")

author: sf-n
body:
This PR adds support for domain sizes and domain inference at compile time. As a result temporary fields are only allocated on the domains that they are read on instead of everywhere.
```python
@gtx.program(static_domains=True)
def testee(...):
        ...
```

Internally compile time domains are realized by the addition of a new argument descriptor `FieldDomainDescriptor` which holds the domain of the corresponding field argument in the form of a `gtx.Domain`. The output domains of `SetAt` statements are replaced with these static domains using the `TransformGetDomainRange` pass introduced in #2151. The domain inference is extended to use the actual values stored in the connectivity to deduce the required domain on which temporaries need to be computed. This domain is potentially non-contiguous and, since we only support contiguous domains, extended to the minimal contiguous domain. In case this extension leads to many unnecessary computations (default is 25% of the total size) a warning is emitted. The current default can be configured by setting `NON_CONTIGUOUS_DOMAIN_WARNING_THRESHOLD` in `gt4py.next.iterator.ir_utils.domain_utils`. The old behavior to compute everywhere is still used in case either a) the `static_domain` option is `False` or b) the backend is configured to compute everywhere by setting `use_max_domain_range_on_unstructured_shift` to `True` in `GTFNTranslationStep` or `DaCeTranslator`.

Note that compile time domains are only supported in `jit` mode right now, as we need to change the `compile` interface, which will happen in a later PR.

# Add HMAC signing support to SDK for API nodes ## Summary This PR implements the final phase of HMAC signing support for API nodes in the Vembda execution path. When API nodes are executed through the Vembda runner instead of the regular workflow runner, they were returning 401 errors because requests weren't being signed with workspace HMAC signatures. **Key Changes:** - Added `workspace_api_key` and `workspace_hmac_secret` parameters to `WorkflowContext` - Implemented HMAC request signing in `BaseAPINode._local_execute_api` method - Created `_sign_request_with_hmac` helper method with proper timestamp and signature generation **Cross-Repository Implementation:** This is part of a three-phase implementation across repositories: 1. **Main Vellum** (PR #12310): Fetch workspace HMAC secret and include in vembda payload ✅ 2. **Vembda-service**: Receive HMAC secret from payload and pass to SDK via WorkflowContext ✅ 3. **SDK** (this PR): Use HMAC secret to sign API requests in BaseAPINode ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **End-to-end verification**: Test that API nodes in vembda runner no longer return 401 errors for workspaces with HMAC signing enabled - [ ] **HMAC signature validation**: Verify the signature format (X-Vellum-Timestamp, X-Vellum-Signature headers) matches existing Vellum HMAC implementation exactly - [ ] **Backward compatibility**: Ensure SDK still works when `workspace_hmac_secret` is None or not provided - [ ] **Security review**: Validate that workspace HMAC secrets are properly handled and not logged/exposed - [ ] **Integration test coverage**: Confirm the test updates in main Vellum PR #12310 properly validate the new payload structure **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Deploy all three PRs to staging environment 2. Create a workflow with an API node that requires HMAC signing 3. Execute via regular workflow runner (should work as before) 4. The focus is on validating core logic related to date handling, formatting, and timezone-aware comparisons to ensure correctness and reliability. During test development, several utility functions were refined to align with their intended behavior—particularly those involving date normalization and comparisons. The utilities tested include: currency formatting, category formatting, date calculations (e.g., isSameDay, isDateInCurrentMonth, getFirstDayOfMonth), numeric transformation utilities. Additionally, Jest was configured with TypeScript support and globals to streamline frontend testing. All tests currently pass. **Random Disclaimer:** Installing Jest caused a lot of additions. ## Milestones Unit test implemented to ensure code quality and that it works Updated calculation functions to fix unwarranted bugs ## Resources A code snippet that I used ``` const datesAreOnSameDay = (first, second) => first.getFullYear() === second.getFullYear() && first.getMonth() === second.getMonth() && first.getDate() === second.getDate(); ``` [Also needed UTC help with timezone](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1292394/what-is-the-need-for-the-javascript-function-getutcfullyear) ## Test Plan

author: joeyparrish
body:
There's no requirement that "+" characters not be used in URLs.  In fact, if you start up `python3 -m http.server` and point your browser at `http://localhost:8000/foo+bar?bar+baz=baz+bar`, you'll see every one of those "+" symbols sent directly to the server without encoding at all.

There is an old convention in CGI parameters to turn " " into "+", but proper URL encoding turns " " into "%20".

The URI parser we use was assuming that "+" is always an escaped " ".  So it would decode "+" into " " and then later re-encode it into "%20".

By removing the special treatment of "+" in the URI parser, we make requests to the correct URLs when they involve "+".

Fixes #8713

author: jdbye
body:
This pull request is a little bit more complicated.
The bulk of these changes were made to allow working with (both serializing and deserializing) incomplete datasets, such as what you will get if you are working with the DB export, which is missing certain fields.
Previously Newtonsoft.Json would choke on these because it didn't expect null values. 

That's not a problem if you just work with the DbExportPost class. But since DbExportPost is a completely separate class it's not easy to work with DbExportPost or Post interchangeably in the same code, as may sometimes be needed, and necessitates a lot of redundant code. Converting everything to Post makes it much easier to work with.
Plus you can fill in a lot of the blanks between DbExportPost and Post. Tags can be assigned to tag categories using the tag database, and there are other similar situations. But to do that obviously they must be converted to Post first since DbExportPost has nowhere to store this data.

Rather than initializing the fields to some other non null value, I thought it made more sense to allow the fields to be null as an indicator that the values are missing which can be used in code to treat them a specific way (say for example, don't display those fields in the UI, or don't take them into account when searching metadata)

Two of the commits in particular (cc8228d94727e147ef64fa4432d63c291d339685 and 1e57ec9bd890c4084a731df4d306096e0b48f476) are related to working with deleted posts. In my application, I have functionality to match local images to posts on e621 and fetch their metadata. That becomes difficult when the IQDB search code refuses to return results for deleted posts, and when GetPost/GetPosts strips out the md5 hash and dimensions from the results of deleted posts. 

To support those changes a change to UriConverter (commit bb4ef8eb09530dad32674ca30b39f1cafd102791) was also needed to allow the location to be null, since for deleted posts, it doesn't make sense to have a location set and it would just point to a dead link anyway.
That is also why the new DatabaseExtension field was added to PostFileImage in commit b846ec89eb68b1f71ae2a80ea66eec04e86de2b5. If Location is not set, then we lose this information. Then GetPathExtensionWithoutDot has nothing to return and we run into an issue. So this field is primarily stored so that GetPathExtensionWithoutDot has something to return when Location is not set.

Being able to get this metadata even for deleted posts can be useful in several situations (besides the obvious one of being able to tag your local images)
For example, a lot of the time, posts get deleted because a superior (higher resolution or quality) version was uploaded, and by having the metadata (and by using the Flag API endpoint) a user can be notified that there is a higher quality version available or that the MD5 hash or resolution of their downloaded image doesn't match the metadata (which also probably means that image is a lower quality version than what is available on e621). Just a couple of real world examples off the top of my head.

Anyways, that's the last of my pull requests (at least for now), hope this works better for you :)

body:
## Overview

This PR provides a comprehensive analysis of the Photofield codebase and establishes a clear roadmap for future improvements. It also fixes several critical code quality issues discovered during the analysis.

## What's Changed

### 📋 Strategic Planning
- **Added comprehensive improvement roadmap** (`IMPROVEMENT_ROADMAP.md`) with 12-week implementation timeline
- **Created analysis summary** (`ANALYSIS_SUMMARY.md`) documenting key findings and priorities
- **Added practical implementation guide** (`docs/development/QUICK_START_IMPROVEMENTS.md`) with code examples

### 🐛 Critical Bug Fixes
- **Fixed mutex receiver issue** in `io/mutex/mutex.go` that was causing potential race conditions
  - Changed value receivers to pointer receivers for methods containing `sync.Map`
  - This prevents lock copying and ensures thread safety

### 🔧 Development Infrastructure
- **Added comprehensive linting configuration** (`.golangci.yml`) with production-ready rules
- **Applied code formatting** across multiple layout files using `gofmt`
- **Set up quality gates** for future development

## Key Findings from Analysis

- **19,500+ lines of Go code** with sophisticated photo processing capabilities
- **38 TODO/FIXME items** identified requiring attention
- **Minimal test coverage** (6 test files) with significant gaps
- **Critical Go vet warnings** that could cause runtime issues

## Priority Areas Identified

### 🔥 High Priority (Weeks 1-2)
1. **Code Quality & Technical Debt**
   - Address context.TODO() usage (improper timeout handling)
   - Expand test coverage for core modules
   - Integrate linting into CI pipeline

2. **Testing Infrastructure**
   - Add integration tests for API endpoints
   - Create performance benchmarks
   - Set up test database helpers

### 🚀 Medium Priority (Weeks 3-6)
1. **Performance Optimization**
   - Memory usage profiling and optimization
   - Database query improvements
   - Concurrent processing enhancements

2. **UI/UX Enhancements**
   - Mobile responsiveness improvements
   - Enhanced metadata display
   - Accessibility improvements

### 🔧 Lower Priority (Weeks 7+)
1. **Architecture Improvements**
   - Module interface definitions
   - Plugin architecture for layouts
   - Configuration validation framework

## Immediate Benefits

- ✅ **Eliminated race condition** in mutex implementation
- ✅ **Consistent code formatting** across the codebase  
- ✅ **Comprehensive linting setup** ready for CI integration
- ✅ **Clear development roadmap** with actionable next steps

## Implementation Timeline

The roadmap provides a structured approach to improvements:

1. **Foundation** (Weeks 1-2): Fix critical issues, add linting, improve tests
2. **Quality & Testing** (Weeks 3-6): Expand coverage, optimize performance  
3. **Features & UX** (Weeks 7-10): Enhance user experience, add features
4. **Architecture** (Weeks 11+): Long-term structural improvements

## Next Steps

The most impactful immediate actions would be:

1. **Integrate linting into CI** using the provided `.golangci.yml`
2. **Fix context.TODO() usage** in layout modules (examples provided)
3. **Add test infrastructure** using the helper patterns documented
4. **Address remaining Go vet warnings** systematically

This analysis provides a clear path forward that balances immediate fixes with long-term architectural improvements, ensuring the project continues to scale effectively while maintaining its impressive performance characteristics.

author: oleludwig
body:
This reverts a change from commit dac2ee4f causing some inputs to be processed incorrectly when using a mysql database. \r would not be removed anymore for inputs ending with \r\n because the code would only remove the \n leaving the \r in place. The function mysql_real_escape_string would then replace the \r with \\r causing some nntp commands to be processed incorrectly. For example the input "group x\r\n" would be transformed to "group x\r" which would be transformed to "group x\\r". This would result in searching the group with the name "x\\r" instead of "x".

I don't now the reason for this change in commit dac2ee4f but could not observe any negative side effects from reverting the change. I ran the TLS-tests from the directory unittesting/tls-testing successfully on various Linux and BSD distributions.

I did not add an entry to the changelog because this bug only affects the not yet released version 2.2.

## Summary

Addresses https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/169590, https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/169091, https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/171323

A legitimate flake was occurring for these tests. It was due to `cy.get(ALERT_COUNT)` sometimes picking up the intermediary filter state when switching between viewing open or closed alerts. When on the alerts page, if you are viewing `closed` alerts and want to view `open` alerts (and vice versa), there is a quick flash where for a bit the page is showing both opened and closed. This isn't a bug, just nature of how the filters work.

Because the intention of these tests is not to test the alerts page specifically, just any alerts table instance, I switched to using the rule details alerts table. In the rule details page, you can easily toggle between alert status, skipping over that intermediary step when switching views that sometimes results in the flake. 

Also moved the privileges check test into it's own folder.

body:
## Description

Application latencies are recorded in the metrics collector now by reading the data that gets collected on the TimedStream object. This PR prepares all the plumbing so that in a follow-up PR, when we pass in the TimedStream for readRows and other endpoints that the TimedStream will send the right application latencies measurements to Google Cloud monitoring dashboard.

## Impact

This PR means that in a follow-up PR, all we have to do is pass in the timed stream that the user has access to into the metrics collector and we can expect this timed stream to send the application blocking latencies to the Google Cloud Monitoring dashboard correctly.

## Testing

`test-common/expected-otel-export-input.ts`: The numbers for the test fixtures in this file have changed slightly because they depend on the values in metrics-handler-fixture.ts and those values have changed.

`test-common/metrics-handler-fixture.ts`: The numbers have changed for the metrics collected in this file because test/metrics-collector/metrics-collector.ts test simulates events that now exclude the event that occurs with a call to onRowReachesUser.

`test/metrics-collector/metrics-collector.ts`: This test has changed so that the fakeMethod doesn't call onRowReachesUser anymore because onRowReachesUser doesn't exist and instead a fake application latencies value is provided by a fake user stream.

`test/metrics-collector/typical-method-call.txt`: This fixture needs to change because it records the order of events that have occurred in `test/metrics-collector/metrics-collector.ts` and the order of events that have occurred in `test/metrics-collector/metrics-collector.ts` has changed.

`test/timed-stream.ts`: The user stream in this method now explicitly calls a callback in its transformHook method.

## Additional Information

Next steps:

- For readRows open a PR that sends the user stream to the metrics collector for readRows calls so that application latencies get recorded.

author: pintopirate
body:
Updates the Pinto TVL adapter to include user deposits in the overall TVL.

After discussing with @realdealshaman  in our thread (https://discord.com/channels/823822164956151810/1397579870363713537), we propose that Pinto/Beanstalk should be in the same boat as Synthetix, barring the discussion of whether protocol issued tokens should count towards staking (https://github.com/DefiLlama/DefiLlama-Adapters/discussions/438). Given the goal of the protocol is to create endogenous value from the credit worthiness of the model and its ability to maintain the value target, we feel that not including deposits in TVL by default greatly undermines the success the protocol has in gaining adoption and trust.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The SuperEditor project was failing to compile with the following error:

```
Error CS0433: The type 'EditorWindow' exists in both 'UnityEditor.CoreModule, Version=0.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null' and 'UnityEditor, Version=0.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null'
```

This error occurred in `Editor/_h1/_h2.cs` at line 14 and affected 25+ other files that inherit from or use `EditorWindow`.

## Root Cause

The `.csproj` file was referencing both:
- **Modern modular assemblies** (Unity 6 standard): `UnityEditor.CoreModule.dll`, `UnityEngine.CoreModule.dll`
- **Legacy monolithic assemblies** (deprecated): `UnityEditor.dll`, `UnityEngine.dll`

Both assemblies contain the `EditorWindow` type, causing compiler ambiguity.

## Solution

**Removed conflicting legacy assembly references:**
- `UnityEditor.dll` (Windows & Linux paths)
- `UnityEngine.dll` (Windows & Linux paths)

**Kept only modular assemblies:**
- ✅ UnityEditor.CoreModule.dll
- ✅ UnityEngine.CoreModule.dll  
- ✅ UnityEngine.IMGUIModule.dll
- ✅ UnityEngine.TextRenderingModule.dll
- ✅ UnityEngine.UnityWebRequestModule.dll
- ✅ UnityEngine.UIElementsModule.dll
- ✅ UnityEditor.UIElementsModule.dll

**Added supplementary modular assemblies:**
- ➕ UnityEngine.AssetBundleModule.dll (for AssetDatabase functionality)
- ➕ UnityEngine.JSONSerializeModule.dll (for JSON serialization)

## Impact

- ✅ **Fixes CS0433 compilation error** across all affected files
- ✅ **No code changes required** - purely build configuration fix
- ✅ **Maintains full functionality** through modular assembly references
- ✅ **Follows Unity 6 best practices** for assembly management
- ✅ **Preserves backward compatibility** with the existing `.asmdef` workflow

## Testing

- Project builds successfully both with and without Unity installation
- All existing SuperEditor functionality preserved
- Assembly references properly resolved through modular dependencies

This change aligns the project with Unity 6's modular assembly architecture and eliminates the type conflicts that were preventing successful compilation.

body:
# Pull Request
This pull request introduces a comprehensive enhancement to user authentication and redirection logic across the application. The key changes include the implementation of a `redirectAfterLogin` mechanism to improve user experience by redirecting users back to their intended destination after login, as well as refactoring login-related thunks for better maintainability. Below is a breakdown of the most important changes:

### Authentication and Redirection Enhancements:
* Added a `redirectAfterLogin` state to the `authSlice` and corresponding actions (`setRedirectAfterLogin`, `clearRedirectAfterLogin`) to manage post-login redirection paths (`src/lib/auth/authSlice.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8cf928f4d6a4936441184ce056de68c22cb3ee6d60596134b152decff6df170dR24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8cf928f4d6a4936441184ce056de68c22cb3ee6d60596134b152decff6df170dR33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8cf928f4d6a4936441184ce056de68c22cb3ee6d60596134b152decff6df170dR87-R92) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8cf928f4d6a4936441184ce056de68c22cb3ee6d60596134b152decff6df170dR104-R105).
* Introduced utility functions `useRedirectPath` and `isValidRedirectPath` to determine valid redirect paths and extract them from the current URL (`src/utils/getRedirectPath.ts`, [src/utils/getRedirectPath.tsR1-R28](diffhunk://#diff-eb901bc295c1af9bb71c86bf8ea626718c3875ad349a4b6b2e9aaac391712dd0R1-R28)).
* Updated `LodgeDetailPage` and `TicketDetailPage` to store pending reservation data in `localStorage` and set `redirectAfterLogin` before triggering the login modal (`src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsx`, [src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsxR180-R221](diffhunk://#diff-b5bc77e1fd0a1af9d3b95de179d38f70eaecbff6a4fcbe38d97ef40c19d96558R180-R221), [src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsxR280-R281](diffhunk://#diff-b5bc77e1fd0a1af9d3b95de179d38f70eaecbff6a4fcbe38d97ef40c19d96558R280-R281), [src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsxL560-R640](diffhunk://#diff-b5bc77e1fd0a1af9d3b95de179d38f70eaecbff6a4fcbe38d97ef40c19d96558L560-R640); `src/app/[locale]/ticket/[ticketId]/page.tsx`, [src/app/[locale]/ticket/[ticketId]/page.tsxR356-R372](diffhunk://#diff-1c065efd44e155078d15da67bfd66d6b530f38f46504af2200a51f9080f17b1eR356-R372)).

### Login Flow Refactoring:
* Refactored `loginThunk` and `socialLoginThunk` to use `createAsyncThunk` for better error handling and return values, and updated their usage across the application (`src/lib/auth/loginThunk.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fe2166b9ad5db6039cce4d457208acbf1c660c27f1b4b7e586554dee727933d3R4-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fe2166b9ad5db6039cce4d457208acbf1c660c27f1b4b7e586554dee727933d3L19-R28); `src/lib/auth/socialLoginThunk.ts`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2c4527b9bb3819937aac341a42144c188e21dda2ca022c1ab4730af76a9df807R4-R12) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2c4527b9bb3819937aac341a42144c188e21dda2ca022c1ab4730af76a9df807L16-R31).
* Enhanced the login flow in `LoginPage` to handle `redirectAfterLogin` and pending reservation data, ensuring users are redirected appropriately after login (`src/app/[locale]/login/page.tsx`, [src/app/[locale]/login/page.tsxR26-R28](diffhunk://#diff-869eb45de992a1ca037683886a3b436c82b5545b9459c4c4a6c2c6e510dd3029R26-R28), [src/app/[locale]/login/page.tsxL46-R95](diffhunk://#diff-869eb45de992a1ca037683886a3b436c82b5545b9459c4c4a6c2c6e510dd3029L46-R95), [src/app/[locale]/login/page.tsxL63-R167](diffhunk://#diff-869eb45de992a1ca037683886a3b436c82b5545b9459c4c4a6c2c6e510dd3029L63-R167)).

### Default Values and Error Handling:
* Updated default values for reservation parameters (`adults`, `room`, `children`) to ensure fallback values are applied when parsing reservation data (`src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsx`, [src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsxL141-R153](diffhunk://#diff-b5bc77e1fd0a1af9d3b95de179d38f70eaecbff6a4fcbe38d97ef40c19d96558L141-R153)).
* Added error handling and logging for scenarios where reservation data or redirect paths are invalid (`src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsx`, [src/app/[locale]/lodge/[lodgeId]/page.tsxR180-R221](diffhunk://#diff-b5bc77e1fd0a1af9d3b95de179d38f70eaecbff6a4fcbe38d97ef40c19d96558R180-R221)).

author: ghchinoy
body:
This commit introduces a new "Negative Prompt" feature to the Veo video generation page and includes several layout and styling enhancements.

Key changes include:

- A new text input field on the Veo page allows users to specify concepts, styles, or objects to exclude from the generated video.
- The application state (`VeoState`) and the model request schema (`VideoGenerationRequest`) have been updated to manage the negative prompt value.
- The core model logic (`models/veo.py`) now correctly passes the negative prompt to the Google GenAI SDK as part of the generation configuration.
- The negative prompt is now saved to Firestore as part of the `MediaItem` metadata, ensuring it is persisted with the generated video.
- The Library page has been updated to display the negative prompt in the details view for videos, making the generation parameters clear.
- The "Clear" button on the Veo page now correctly resets the negative prompt field.
- A new automated test (`test/test_veo_negative_prompt.py`) has been added to verify the end-to-end data flow of the negative prompt.
- The contrast for the resolution pills (e.g., "1080p") in the library has been improved for better readability.
- The layout of the Veo page has been made more robust by removing a fixed height on the main controls container, preventing content overflow.
- The text input areas for the prompt and negative prompt now share a consistent, polished style.
- The generated video display is now fully responsive, scaling gracefully with the browser window size.

author: phertyameen
body:
## Description

This PR introduces a self-contained module for tracking and storing mock internet speed test results.

## What's Included

-  **Entity**:
  - `InternetSpeedTest`: includes `location`, `downloadSpeed`, `uploadSpeed`, and `timestamp`

-  **Endpoints**:
  - `POST /speed-test`: Record a new mock speed test result
  - `GET /speed-test`: Fetch all test results
  - `GET /speed-test/filter`: Query results by location and/or timestamp

-  **Features**:
  - Ability to store and retrieve mock internet speed results
  - Query filters for better insights (e.g., view speeds for a given location or date)
  - Swagger decorators and API documentation for all routes and DTOs

## Highlights

-  Fully isolated from other modules
-  Easily extensible to integrate real speed test APIs
-  Includes validation and error handling for inputs

## How to Test

1. Run `POST /speed-test` with test data (location, uploadSpeed, downloadSpeed)
2. Use `GET /speed-test` to retrieve all test entries
3. Use `GET /speed-test/filter?location=X&date=YYYY-MM-DD` to filter results

Closes issue #93

author: lritzdorf
body:
Magellan already accounts for a complication where some BMCs expose their ComputerSystems under `/redfish/v1/Chassis` instead of `.../Systems`.,However, the existing logic just concatenates the two sets of ComputerSystems found in this way, which is a problem if the same systems are exposed under each of the two endpoints — we end up with two entries for each system. (Confusingly, pairs entries are not actually identical; ones from the `Systems` endpoint may be missing chassis information.)

This PR adds logic to merge duplicate ComputerSystems from the two endpoints. Duplicate systems found in `Systems` are merged onto their counterparts from `Chassis`, i.e. any non-empty fields override their existing counterparts. (The `Systems` endpoint is the canonical location for ComputerSystems, so entries from there get priority.)

Also, another included commit fixes a CLI-binding typo for the access token flag.

author: rosscado
body:
Adds dictation mode support for **Lexical rich text editors**, enabling voice input compatibility with Meta products (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp Web) and **Perplexity AI**.

## Key Changes

### 🎯 **Lexical Editor Detection & Insertion**
- Detects Lexical editors via `data-lexical-editor="true"` attribute
- Implements proper text insertion using `InputEvent` with `insertText` type
- Ensures compatibility with Lexical's event-driven architecture

### 🏗️ **Strategy Pattern Refactoring**
- Refactored `setTextInTarget()` using strategy pattern for better maintainability
- **`LexicalEditorStrategy`**: Handles Lexical rich text editors
- **`InputTextareaStrategy`**: Handles `<input>` and `<textarea>` elements  
- **`ContentEditableStrategy`**: Handles standard `contenteditable` elements
- **`TextInsertionStrategySelector`**: Automatically selects appropriate strategy

### 🐛 **Bug Fixes**
- Fixed transcription duplication on first utterance in Lexical editors
- Improved deduplication logic to prevent content repetition
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing editor types

## Testing
- ✅ All 191 existing tests pass
- ✅ Preserves functionality for standard inputs, textareas, and contenteditable elements
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing dictation behavior

## Impact
Users can now dictate into Lexical-based editors including:
- **Perplexity AI** prompt box

author: milicaradicc
body:
This PR introduces comprehensive chat functionality to the EventPlanner Android app, enabling real-time messaging between users through REST API calls and WebSocket connections. The implementation provides a seamless chat experience with contact management and live message updates.

---

## Key Features

### Real-time Messaging
- **WebSocket Integration**: STOMP client implementation for real-time message exchange.
- **Dual Communication**: Messages sent via both REST API and WebSocket for reliability.
- **Live Updates**: Real-time message reception through STOMP topic subscription `/socket-publisher/{userId}`.
- **Message Persistence**: All messages stored and retrieved via REST API calls.

### Contact Management
- **Horizontal Contact List**: Clean, scrollable contact display in RecyclerView.
- **Contact Selection**: Tap-to-chat functionality with automatic message loading.
- **Dynamic Loading**: Contacts fetched and displayed dynamically.

### Message Display
- **Differentiated UI**: Distinct layouts for sent vs received messages.
- **User-Aware Styling**: Messages styled based on current user context.
- **Smooth Scrolling**: Optimized RecyclerView performance for message lists.

---

## Technical Implementation

### Network Layer
- **MessageService**: Retrofit interface with endpoints:
  - `GET /messages` - Fetch conversation messages.
  - `POST /messages` - Send new messages.
  - `GET /chat-contacts` - Retrieve chat contact list.
- **ClientUtils Integration**: MessageService registered in existing client architecture.
- **STOMP WebSocket**: Real-time bidirectional communication setup.

### Architecture Components
- **ChatViewModel**: Manages state for message loading/sending, contact list, WebSocket lifecycle, and real-time updates.
- **ChatFragment**: Handles contact selection, message display, message input, sending, and WebSocket subscription.

### UI Components
- **ChatAdapter**: Displays messages with sent/received differentiation and smooth scrolling.
- **ChatContactAdapter**: Displays horizontal contact list with selection handling and efficient view recycling.

---

## Data Models

### DTO Classes
- **GetMessageDTO**: Message retrieval data structure.
- **CreateMessageDTO**: Message creation payload.
- **CreatedMessageDTO**: Message creation response.
- **GetChatContact**: Contact information structure.

---

## UI/UX Design

### Layout Files
- **`fragment_chat.xml`**: Main chat layout with horizontal RecyclerView for contacts, vertical RecyclerView for messages, and message input.
- **`item_message_sent.xml`**: Right-aligned sent message bubble.
- **`item_message_received.xml`**: Left-aligned received message bubble.
- **`item_chat_contact.xml`**: Contact list item with profile display and selection states.

### Design Principles
- Intuitive navigation with clear visual hierarchy.
- Responsive design for various screen sizes.
- Consistent styling following app design system.
- Accessibility with proper content descriptions and touch targets.

---

## Real-time Communication Flow

### WebSocket Integration
1. STOMP client connects on chat initialization.
2. Subscribe to user-specific topic for incoming messages.
3. Sent messages broadcast through WebSocket.
4. Incoming messages automatically update UI.

### Message Lifecycle
1. **Send**: REST API call + WebSocket broadcast.
2. **Receive**: WebSocket subscription + UI update.
3. **Persistence**: All messages stored via backend API.
4. **Loading**: Historical messages loaded via REST API

author: philly-zion
body:
### **Description**

This pull request introduces the **initial core implementation** of the StackCredit protocol — a decentralized credit scoring and lending system built on **Stacks Layer 2**, secured by Bitcoin. The contract supports on-chain credit profiling, dynamic loan issuance, adaptive collateralization, interest rate logic, and full loan lifecycle management.

Key functionality includes:

* User onboarding and credit profile initialization
* Loan requests with dynamic collateral and rate determination based on credit score
* Partial and full loan repayment with automatic collateral release and score updates
* Administrative handling of loan defaults with penalties
* Internal score recalculation logic and risk-based borrowing incentives
* Read-only access to user, loan, and system metrics

---

### **Key Changes**

* **Data Models:**

  * `UserScores`: Tracks credit score, history, and performance metrics
  * `Loans`: Records individual loan metadata and repayment status
  * `UserLoans`: Associates users with their active loans
* **State Variables:**

  * `next-loan-id`, `total-stx-locked`
* **Public Functions:**

  * `initialize-score`: Initializes a new user profile
  * `request-loan`: Handles dynamic collateralized loan issuance
  * `repay-loan`: Allows repayment and updates credit scores
  * `mark-loan-defaulted`: Admin-only function for overdue loans
* **Private Logic Helpers:**

  * `calculate-required-collateral`: Computes collateral based on score
  * `calculate-interest-rate`: Calculates interest from credit score
  * `calculate-total-due`: Returns principal + interest
  * `update-credit-score`: Modifies score based on repayment/default
  * `update-user-loans`: Tracks active loan IDs per user
* **Read-Only Interfaces:**

  * `get-user-score`, `get-loan`, `get-user-active-loans`, `get-system-stats`

---

### **Impact**

This lays the foundation for StackCredit’s credit-based DeFi ecosystem by:

* Reducing the reliance on overcollateralization
* Incentivizing responsible borrowing via on-chain reputation
* Enabling trustless lending directly on Bitcoin via Stacks

It provides a fully transparent, extensible credit layer for integration into broader Bitcoin-native DeFi apps.

---

### **Next Steps**

* Integrate front-end dApp interface and wallet interactions
* Add unit tests and edge-case coverage
* Implement loan liquidation and collateral auction module
* Extend scoring logic with time-weighted repayment history

---

### **Reviewer Notes**

* Focus on logic correctness and security of `request-loan` and `repay-loan`
* Validate math on `calculate-required-collateral` and interest rate calculations
* Confirm edge cases for credit score boundaries (min/max)

body:
## Summary

This PR resolves a critical bug where the system incorrectly threw `DuplicateAttributeDefinitionError` when users legitimately defined attributes in their configuration that existed from previous deployments.

**Issue**: Users encountered false positive errors claiming attributes were "already defined elsewhere in the configuration" when they were actually only defined once in their current config file.

**Root Cause**: The validation logic in `ProductTypeService.createAttributes()` was too strict, throwing errors whenever it found any existing attribute globally, even in legitimate scenarios where users were simply updating or reusing attributes from previous deployments.

## Changes Made

- **Modified ProductTypeService.createAttributes()**: Changed the logic to reuse existing global attributes instead of throwing duplicate errors
- **Updated test coverage**: Added comprehensive tests covering the bug scenario and updated existing tests to reflect the new permissive behavior
- **Improved attribute handling**: System now intelligently reuses existing attributes rather than failing with misleading error messages

## Test Plan

To reproduce and verify the fix:

1. **Setup**: Delete any existing config file
   ```bash
   rm -f config.yml
   ```

2. **Introspect**: Get current Saleor configuration
   ```bash
   pnpm run introspect --url https://your-store.saleor.cloud --token your-token
   ```

3. **Modify**: Add an attribute to any product type in `config.yml`:
   ```yaml
   productTypes:

author: paulrbr
body:
This commit allows server URLs in the JWT payload to include server
variables (in the OpenAPI meaning) and replaces those by `.*` regepx
wildcards

Meaning that a server url of `https://{cluster}.{region}.example.com`
will be transformed into `https://.*..*.example.com` and be used to
match the target URL of the proxied request.

Note: the verification checks that the server variables are part of
the two last segments of the server url (meaning the server url MUST
end with a domain name and a TLD)

author: albeanth
body:
## What is the change? Why is it being made?

These changes support the ongoing the multi-pin assembly effort.

The current axial expansion changer was built assuming there would be a single pin type. When introducing a second pin type (presumably fuel or other neutronically important material) it is no longer generally possible to conserve mass of the second pin component who is the non-axial expansion target component. The lone exception is if the second component is isothermal and contains the same number densities throughout. 

To address this limitation, this PR improves on the mass redistribution that was previously implicitly done by explicitly passing mass between axially linked components and using this new mass and volume to compute new number densities. This new redistribution requires that the axially linked components have the same nuclides; this is used to ensure that they are the same material. If the nuclides were different, they would presumably be different materials and material properties would become largely unknown. 

### High-level description of changes:

1. `assemblyAxialLinkage.py`: bring back upper
2. `axialExpansionChanger`: new redistrubtion algorithm
3. `expansionData: add `getTargetComponent` method
4. `test_axialExpansionChanger.py`: add tests
5. `densityTools.py`: type hints
6. `detailedAxialExpansion` blueprints: simplify simplify simplify

## SCR Information

Change Type: features

One-Sentence Description:  New axial expansion changer that manually redistributes mass. 

One-line Impact on Requirements: Minor change to the implementation `I_ARMI_INP_COLD_HEIGHT` for `R_ARMI_INP_COLD_HEIGHT` and major change to the implementation `I_ARMI_ASSEM_HEIGHT_PRES` for `R_ARMI_ASSEM_HEIGHT_PRES`; adding logic for block-level mass redistribution.

This PR is part 1 of adding a visualization that allows us to inspect the hypothesis space at every step of every episode for a Monty unsupervised inference experiment.

In this PR, I'm adding the code for logging resampling statistics such as which hypotheses have been added or removed at every step, the evidence values, slopes and ages, rotations, pose errors, etc.

Since this is a lot of information that we're logging I added a `ResamplingHypothesesUpdater` flag named `save_stats` which must be set to true in the configs to save all this extra logging information. This is similar to `save_raw_obs` for the SMs.

In a follow up PR, I will add the interactive visualization to make use of this logged information.

body:
This PR simplifies the Azure deployment workflow by removing conditional logic from the authentication step and consolidating to a single login method.

## Changes Made

- **Removed conditional** `if: ${{ env.AZURE_CLIENT_ID != '' }}` from the Federated Credentials login step
- **Removed entire Client Credentials login step** that used `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` secret
- **Cleaned up unused environment variable** `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` that was no longer referenced
- **Simplified authentication flow** to use only Federated Credentials method

## Before
The workflow had two conditional login steps:
```yaml
- name: Log in with Azure (Federated Credentials)
  if: ${{ env.AZURE_CLIENT_ID != '' }}
  # ... federated credentials logic

- name: Log in with Azure (Client Credentials)
  if: ${{ env.AZURE_CREDENTIALS != '' }}
  # ... client credentials logic
```

## After
The workflow now has a single unconditional login step:
```yaml
- name: Log in with Azure (Federated Credentials)
  run: |
    azd auth login `
      --client-id "$Env:AZURE_CLIENT_ID" `
      --federated-credential-provider "github" `
      --tenant-id "$Env:AZURE_TENANT_ID"
  shell: pwsh
```

## Benefits

- **Simplified workflow logic** - no more conditional branching
- **Reduced complexity** - fewer potential failure points
- **Consistent authentication method** - always uses Federated Credentials
- **Follows current best practices** for Azure authentication in GitHub Actions
- **Cleaner configuration** - removed unused environment variables

The changes are minimal (16 lines removed, 0 lines added) and maintain full functionality while improving maintainability.

Fixes #66.

<summary>shlinkio/shlink (ghcr.io/shlinkio/shlink)</summary>

### [`v4.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#450---2025-07-24)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/compare/v4.4.6...v4.5.0)

##### Added

- [#​2438](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2438) Add `MERCURE_ENABLED` env var and corresponding config option, to more easily allow the mercure integration to be toggled.

  For BC, if this env var is not present, we'll still consider the integration enabled if the `MERCURE_PUBLIC_HUB_URL` env var has a value. This is considered deprecated though, and next major version will rely only on `MERCURE_ENABLED`, so if you are using Mercure, make sure to set `MERCURE_ENABLED=true` to be ready.

- [#​2387](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2387) Add `REAL_TIME_UPDATES_TOPICS` env var and corresponding config option, to granularly decide which real-time updates topics should be enabled.

- [#​2418](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2418) Add more granular control over how Shlink handles CORS. It is now possible to customize the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Max-Age` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` headers via env vars or config options.

- [#​2386](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2386) Add new `any-value-query-param` and `valueless-query-param` redirect rule conditions.

  These new rules expand the existing `query-param`, which requires both a specific non-empty value in order to match the condition.

  The new conditions match as soon as a query param exists with any or no value (in the case of `any-value-query-param`), or if a query param exists with no value at all (in the case of `valueless-query-param`).

- [#​2360](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2360) Add `TRUSTED_PROXIES` env var and corresponding config option, to configure a comma-separated list of all the proxies in front of Shlink, or simply the amount of trusted proxies in front of Shlink.

  This is important to properly detect visitor's IP addresses instead of incorrectly matching one of the proxy's IP address, and if provided, it disables a workaround introduced in [https://github.com/shlinkio/shlink/pull/2359](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/pull/2359).

- [#​2274](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2274) Add more supported device types for the `device` redirect condition:

  - `linux`: Will match desktop devices with Linux.
  - `windows`: Will match desktop devices with Windows.
  - `macos`: Will match desktop devices with MacOS.
  - `chromeos`: Will match desktop devices with ChromeOS.
  - `mobile`: Will match any mobile devices with either Android or iOS.

- [#​2093](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2093) Add `REDIRECT_CACHE_LIFETIME` env var and corresponding config option, so that it is possible to set the `Cache-Control` visibility directive (`public` or `private`) when the `REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE` has been set to `301` or `308`.

- [#​2323](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2323) Add `LOGS_FORMAT` env var and corresponding config option, to allow the logs generated by Shlink to be in console or JSON formats.

- [#​2406](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2406) Remove references to bootstrap from error templates, and instead inline the very minimum required styles.

- [#​2408](https://redirect.github.com/shlinkio/shlink/issues/2408) Generating QR codes via `/{short-code}/qr-code` is now deprecated and will be removed in Shlink 5.0. Use the equivalent capability from web clients instead.

author: semeberry
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based system for managing advanced materials and nanotechnology development using Clarity smart contracts on the Stacks blockchain. The system provides end-to-end functionality for material verification, safety assessment, deployment coordination, manufacturing management, and composite optimization.

## Features Implemented

### 1. Metamaterial Property Verification Contract
- **Material Registration**: Register engineered materials with novel physical properties
- **Verification System**: Multi-verifier approval process with configurable thresholds
- **Property Analysis**: Calculate strength-to-weight ratios and performance scores
- **Authorization Management**: Role-based access control for verifiers

### 2. Nanoparticle Safety Assessment Contract
- **Particle Registration**: Register nanoparticles with size and composition data
- **Safety Assessment**: Comprehensive toxicity evaluation (cytotoxicity, genotoxicity, etc.)
- **Exposure Tracking**: Monitor health impacts and exposure records
- **Environmental Impact**: Assess aquatic toxicity, soil persistence, and bioaccumulation

This PR implements comprehensive improvements to the Classic Memory mode as requested in the issue, transforming it from a basic 5-round progressive grid system to an enhanced 10-round experience with consistent layout and detailed scoring.

## Changes Implemented

### 1. Grid Layout Standardization
- **Changed from progressive grids to consistent 6×5 layout** for all rounds
- Previously: 3×4, 4×4, 4×5, 5×5, 5×6 grids across 5 rounds
- Now: 6×5 grid (6 columns, 5 rows) for all 10 rounds
- Progressive difficulty through pair count (4-15 pairs) rather than grid size changes

### 2. Extended Game Duration
- **Increased from 5 to 10 rounds** for longer gameplay
- Progressive pair counts: starts with 4 pairs in round 1, increases to 15 pairs by round 10
- Game ends immediately if player fails to complete all pairs within the 30-second time limit

### 3. Enhanced Score Table
- **Replaced generic game over overlay** with detailed score table
- Shows **round-by-round performance** with individual scores
- Displays **total score** and high score information
- Proper "GAME COMPLETE!" messaging

### 4. Improved Navigation
- **Removed Restart and Back buttons** during gameplay (kept only QUIT)
- **Added AGAIN and MENU buttons** to score table:
  - AGAIN: Restarts Classic Memory game
  - MENU: Returns to mode selection
  - QUIT: Returns to main menu (positioned at bottom)
- Buttons are **centered horizontally** as requested

### 5. Confirmed Existing Features
- ✅ **No question marks on tiles** (tiles display as blank gray squares when face down)
- ✅ Clean interface with minimal button clutter during gameplay

## Technical Implementation

```javascript

function getClassicRoundGrid(round) {
  const pairs = Math.min(15, 3 + round); // Progressive pairs: 4-15
  return { rows: 5, cols: 6, pairs: pairs };
}

  // ... rest of initialization
}

};
```

author: willhickey
body:
#### Problem
Many operators use systemd to run Agave. A very common restart sequence is:
`agave-validator exit && systemctl restart`

The `exit` command here returns after sending an exit request to the validator, but it doesn't wait for the validator to finish exiting†. Thus `systemctl restart` runs before the validator has shutdown. `systemctl restart` sends `SIGTERM` immediately. If the process is still running after `TimeoutStopSec` seconds it sends `SIGKILL`.

the `SIGTERM` often leads to ungraceful exits. This is suboptimal, but has recently become particularly problematic in the specific case of downgrading from v2.3 to v2.2 (see discussions in Discord [#validator-support](https://discord.com/channels/428295358100013066/560174212967432193/1397600439356362794) and [#releng](https://discord.com/channels/428295358100013066/910937142182682656/1397661826656895016)).

† a `--wait-for-exit` flag has been added in PR #6780 but that change is not in v2.2.

#### Summary of Changes
Add a `SIGTERM` handler that initiates a graceful shutdown.


#### Testing
on `shared-dev8` I tested downgrading this PR branch to v2.2.20:
* Get `agave-validator` running against testnet from `fa6b70d6`
* `agave-install init v2.2.20` to switch my local pathed version to v2.2.20
* `agave-validator exit && ./restart`
Here are some select lines from `~/logs/agave-validator.log`. Note that `SIGTERM` is received 4.6s before the validator ultimately exits gracefully
```

[2025-07-25T16:29:37.139315658Z INFO  solana_core::snapshot_packager_service] Received exit request, tearing down...

[2025-07-25T16:29:42.449708304Z INFO  agave_validator] agave-validator 2.2.20 (src:dabc99a5; feat:3073396398, client:Agave)
```

## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

We think it would be reasonable to bump OM and SCM Ratis (Raft) segment size (`ozone.om.ratis.segment.size` and `ozone.scm.ha.ratis.segment.size`) default values from `4MB` to `64MB`. We are already using `64MB` on DNs for about 2 years:

https://github.com/apache/ozone/commit/fbe584c0cc6e33b737b9b6cf31ee592018d8e594

`ozone.om.ratis.segment.size` sets the size of the raft segment used by Apache Ratis on OM.

`ozone.scm.ha.ratis.segment.size` sets the size of the raft segment used by Apache Ratis on SCM.

`dfs.container.ratis.segment.size` sets the size of the raft segment used by Apache Ratis on DN.
