This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.2.1** to **7.10.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_ and duplicate `issue 378`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes
  `issue 831`_.

- A new command-line option: ``--save-signal=USR1`` specifies a signal that
  coverage.py will listen for.  When the signal is sent, the coverage data will
  be saved.  This makes it possible to save data from within long-running
  processes.  Thanks, `Arkady Gilinsky <pull 1998_>`_.

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_report_partial_also`" is a list of
  regexes to add as pragmas for partial branches.  This parallels the
  ":ref:`config_report_exclude_also`" setting for adding line exclusion
  patterns.

- A few file path configuration settings didn't allow for tilde expansion:
  :ref:`config_json_output`, :ref:`config_lcov_output` and
  :ref:`config_run_debug_file`.  This is now fixed.

- Wheels are included for 3.14 now that 3.14 rc1 is available.

- We no longer ship a PyPy-specific wheel. PyPy will install the pure-Python
  wheel.  Closes `issue 2001`_.

- In the very unusual situation of not having a current frame, coverage no
  longer crashes when using the sysmon core, fixing `issue 2005`_.

.. _issue 43: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/43
.. _issue 310: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/310
.. _issue 312: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/312

   ### 7.9.2

   --------------------------

- Fix: complex conditionals within a line might cause a KeyError when using
  sys.monitoring, as reported in `issue 1991`_.  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we can now measure coverage for code in Python archive (.par) files.
  Thanks, `Itamer Oren <pull 1984_>`_.

.. _pull 1984: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1984
.. _issue 1991: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1991

  your configuration.  Plugins and dynamic contexts are still not supported

  1977`_.  Thanks, `Adam Turner <pull 1978_>`_.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Google Play packaging was failing when domains contained Java keywords like 'new', resulting in invalid package names. For example, the domain `new.kpr-co.com` would generate the package ID `com.kpr_co.new.twa`, which is invalid because `new` is a reserved Java keyword.

The error message from the Android build system was:
```
Namespace 'com.kpr_co.new.twa' is not a valid Java package name as 'new' is a Java keyword.
```

## Solution

Modified the `generatePackageId` function in `android-validation.ts` to detect Java keywords and append an underscore to make them valid Java identifiers.

### Key Changes

1. **Added comprehensive Java keyword list**: All 54 Java keywords are now handled
2. **Implemented `avoidJavaKeywords()` helper**: Appends `_` suffix to any Java keyword
3. **Enhanced validation**: Added validation to catch manually entered Java keywords
4. **Minimal and surgical fix**: Only modifies domain parts that are actually Java keywords

### Examples

**Original failing case:**
```
Input:  new.kpr-co.com
Before: com.kpr_co.new.twa     ❌ (contains Java keyword 'new')
After:  com.kpr_co.new_.twa    ✅ (valid Java package name)
```

**Multiple keywords:**
```
Input:  new.if.complex.com
Output: com.complex.if_.new_.twa    ✅
```

**Non-keywords unchanged:**
```
Input:  example.com
Output: com.example.twa    ✅ (no change needed)
```

### Backward Compatibility

- ✅ Preserves all existing functionality (leading digit handling, character replacement)
- ✅ Normal domains continue to work exactly as before
- ✅ Existing validation rules remain in place
- ✅ No breaking changes to the API

### Testing

Added comprehensive test suite with 11 test cases covering:
- Original failing case
- Multiple Java keywords in same domain
- Various individual keywords (if, class, interface, public, static, etc.)
- Edge cases with special characters and numbers
- Normal domains to ensure no regression

The fix is minimal and surgical, resolving the Google Play packaging failure while maintaining the existing codebase's robustness and functionality.

Fixes #5024.

author: thingersoft
body:
This merge request addresses several security issues identified in the codebase:

1. **XML Parser Security**: Configures `DocumentBuilderFactory` to disallow DOCTYPE declarations and disable external entity processing, protecting against XXE attacks. Features set:
   - `factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true)`
   - `factory.setFeature("http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities", false)`
   - `factory.setFeature("http://xml.org/sax/features/external-parameter-entities", false)`
2. **Safe Transformer Configuration**: Ensures `TransformerFactory` disallows access to external DTDs and stylesheets by setting the `accessExternalDTD` and `accessExternalStylesheet` attributes to empty strings.
3. **Actuator Exposure Restriction**: Removes/restricts full actuator endpoint exposure or ensures that such exposure is protected by appropriate authentication mechanisms.

After these changes, all previously identified security issues have been resolved (no remaining flagged issues). This merge will substantially improve the application's security profile.

*Please review and approve for merging into the main branch.*

## Problem
The current instruction text for downloading ATAK/iTAK apps was somewhat awkward and redundant:
> "Need to install ATAK or iTAK? Use the links below to install them."

## Solution
Updated to more user-friendly and actionable language:
> "Don't have ATAK or iTAK installed? Download from your device's app store:"

## Changes
- `src/enrollment-lambda/views/partials/store_badges.ejs`: Updated instruction text

## Benefits
- **More conversational tone** - "Don't have" sounds more natural than "Need to install"
- **Clearer action** - "Download from your device's app store" is more specific than "Use the links below"
- **Better flow** - Removes redundancy ("install" appeared twice in original)
- **Device-agnostic** - Works for both Android and iOS users
- **Shorter and cleaner** - More concise while maintaining clarity

Minor UX improvement for the device enrollment flow.

body:
## Description

**parameter change [PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1574) should be merged first**

This PR enhances the vehicle command filter by adding lateral jerk constraint functionality to the steering rate limiting mechanism. The enhancement improves vehicle stability and comfort by dynamically adjusting steering rate limits based on vehicle speed and lateral jerk constraints.

### Key Changes:

- Added `lat_jerk_lim_for_steer_rate` parameter to both nominal and transition operation modes
- Enhanced `limitLateralSteerRate` function to apply the more restrictive limit between basic steering rate and lateral jerk constraints
- Implemented physics-based calculation using the formula: `j_y = (1/L) * V^2 * (dθ/dt)`
- Added comprehensive test coverage for the new functionality

#### Additions

| Change type | Parameter Name                              | Type     | Default Value | Description                                                                                 |
| :---------- | :------------------------------------------ | :------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Added       | `nominal.lat_jerk_lim_for_steer_rate`       | `double` | `10.0`        | Limit for lateral jerk constraint on steering rate (activated in AUTONOMOUS operation mode) |
| Added       | `on_transition.lat_jerk_lim_for_steer_rate` | `double` | `10.0`        | Limit for lateral jerk constraint on steering rate (activated in TRANSITION operation mode) |

## Effects on system behavior

**Improved Vehicle Stability**: The lateral jerk constraint provides more sophisticated steering rate limiting that adapts to vehicle speed, resulting in:

- Smoother steering behavior at high speeds
- Better passenger comfort through reduced lateral jerk
- Maintained agility at low speeds where higher steering rates are safe

body:
This PR completes the road quality mapping application for cataloging bike ride road quality using smartphone sensors, implementing all requirements from the project specification.

## 🚴‍♂️ Main Application Interface
![Main Application](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f49e80e-4b91-4afb-99f8-50f8-647fe0d8)

## 🧪 Testing Interface  
![Test Page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/999a0528-6f52-4b13-b1f8-56e8be6ac176)

## ✨ Key Features Implemented

### **Real-time Road Quality Recording**
- Uses device GPS and accelerometer to record road vibrations at high frequency
- Analyzes data in 200-meter segments (upgraded from 50m as required)
- Color-codes route segments based on road roughness scores
- Automatically exports data to Firebase at end of recording

### **Smart Vibration Filtering**
Implements advanced filtering to remove non-road movements:
```javascript
// Filters out phone handling, braking, acceleration
function filterVibration(magnitude, timestamp) {
    const baseline = 9.8; // gravity baseline
    const deviation = Math.abs(magnitude - baseline);
    
    // Filter extreme values (phone handling)
    if (deviation > 15) return 0;
    
    // High-pass filter for road-specific vibrations
    return Math.max(0, deviation - movingAverageBaseline);
}
```

### **Firebase Integration**
- Stores road quality data with GPS coordinates
- Loads and displays previous ride data on map
- Overwrites quality scores for previously covered locations
- Handles data persistence and synchronization

### **Dual Operating Modes**
1. **Real Recording Mode**: Live sensor data collection during bike rides
2. **Simulation Mode**: GPX file testing for development/demonstration

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### **Device Sensor Access**
- **GPS**: High-accuracy geolocation tracking
- **Accelerometer**: Motion data collection with permission handling
- **iOS 13+ Support**: Proper motion permission requests

### **Data Processing**
- **200m Segmentation**: Non-overlapping analysis windows
- **RMS Calculation**: Root Mean Square for road roughness scoring
- **Real-time Processing**: Live quality assessment and visualization

### **User Interface**
- **Live Map Display**: Shows current route with quality color-coding
- **Historical Overlay**: Displays previous Firebase data as context
- **Recording Controls**: Start/stop buttons for both modes
- **Vibration Preview**: Chart showing upcoming segment data

## 📱 Usage

### Real Recording
```javascript
// Start recording with device sensors
document.getElementById('startRecordingBtn').click();
// Bike ride with phone - app automatically processes data
// Stop recording to save to Firebase
document.getElementById('stopRecordingBtn').click();
```

### Simulation Testing
```javascript
// Upload GPX file and simulate movement
document.getElementById('gpxInput').files = [gpxFile];
document.getElementById('startBtn').click();
```

## 🧪 Testing & Validation

Added comprehensive test suite (`test.html`) that validates:
- GPS functionality
- Accelerometer data collection
- Vibration filtering algorithms
- Firebase connectivity
- End-to-end recording simulation

## 📁 Files Changed

### Core Application
- **`app.js`**: Enhanced with real sensor data, Firebase integration, filtering algorithms
- **`index.html`**: Added recording buttons and Firebase SDK imports  
- **`style.css`**: Updated styling for new UI elements

### Configuration & Documentation
- **`firebase-config.js`**: Easy Firebase setup configuration
- **`test.html`**: Comprehensive testing interface
- **`README.md`**: Complete setup and usage documentation

## 🚀 Setup Instructions

1. **Configure Firebase**: Edit `firebase-config.js` with your project settings
2. **Enable Firestore**: Set up database in Firebase Console
3. **Serve over HTTPS**: Required for sensor access (or use localhost for development)
4. **Mobile Device**: Best experience on smartphones/tablets with GPS and accelerometer

## ✅ Requirements Fulfilled

- ✅ High-frequency vibration recording and analysis
- ✅ GPS coordinate tracking for road localization  
- ✅ 200-meter segment analysis windows
- ✅ Road quality scoring and color-coding
- ✅ Firebase data export and storage
- ✅ Previous data loading and display
- ✅ Location-based data overwriting
- ✅ Live map display with quality visualization
- ✅ Vibration filtering for non-road movements

The application is now fully functional for real-world road quality mapping during bike rides, meeting all specified requirements with robust testing and comprehensive documentation.

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.4** to **7.10.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_ and duplicate `issue 378`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes
  `issue 831`_.

- A new command-line option: ``--save-signal=USR1`` specifies a signal that
  coverage.py will listen for.  When the signal is sent, the coverage data will
  be saved.  This makes it possible to save data from within long-running
  processes.  Thanks, `Arkady Gilinsky <pull 1998_>`_.

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_report_partial_also`" is a list of
  regexes to add as pragmas for partial branches.  This parallels the
  ":ref:`config_report_exclude_also`" setting for adding line exclusion
  patterns.

- A few file path configuration settings didn't allow for tilde expansion:
  :ref:`config_json_output`, :ref:`config_lcov_output` and
  :ref:`config_run_debug_file`.  This is now fixed.

- Wheels are included for 3.14 now that 3.14 rc1 is available.

- We no longer ship a PyPy-specific wheel. PyPy will install the pure-Python
  wheel.  Closes `issue 2001`_.

- In the very unusual situation of not having a current frame, coverage no
  longer crashes when using the sysmon core, fixing `issue 2005`_.

   --------------------------

- Fix: complex conditionals within a line might cause a KeyError when using

- Fix: we can now measure coverage for code in Python archive (.par) files.
  Thanks, `Itamer Oren <pull 1984_>`_.

.. _pull 1984: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1984

   --------------------------

- The "no-ctracer" warning is not issued for Python pre-release versions.

- On Python 3.14+, the "sysmon" core is now the default if it's supported for

   --------------------------

body:
## What?
- Added a new test `test_add_product_to_open_order_not_closed` in order.py to verify that adding products to cart creates new open orders instead of adding to closed orders

## Why?
- To ensure proper order state management in the e-commerce system
- To validate that customers can continue shopping after completing purchases without affecting their purchase history
- To prevent business logic bugs where new cart items could be added to completed orders
- To fulfill the requirement: "Create a new test that verifies that adding a product to the user's cart adds it to an open order, and not a closed one"

## How?
- Created a comprehensive test that simulates a complete purchase cycle:
  1. Creates a payment type with required fields (`merchant_name`, `account_number`, `expiration_date`, `create_date`)
  2. Adds a product to cart (creates first open order)
  3. Completes the purchase by adding payment type (closes the order)
  4. Adds another product to cart (should create a new open order)
  5. Verifies that a new order was created with a different ID
  6. Confirms the new order is open (`payment_type = null`)
  7. Validates that the customer now has 2 total orders

## Testing?
- Test passes successfully with `poetry run python manage.py test tests.order.OrderTests.test_add_product_to_open_order_not_closed`
- Validates core business logic: shopping carts always work with open orders, never closed ones
- Ensures proper separation between active shopping sessions and completed purchases
- Confirms database integrity by verifying order counts and states

author: michaing
body:
Test builds: https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/actions/runs/16510133216

### Our package has a few differences compared to the Debian package:
- It does not have the Python module option enabled, which is using `python` keyword in `module-config:` setting, and defining a `python-script:` to be called along the processing chain. If anyone is actually making use of this, we can compile it in, but calling Python scripts along DNS query processing sounds like a very inefficient and slowing-down procedure, so I would be very interested of the use case then. Not compiling it in gets rid of Python dependency of our package.
- It does not have the AppArmor profile from the Debian package included. If someone uses AppArmor and finds that valuable enough, we can add it, but it would prefer to instead add sandboxing via systemd unit, which is done [upstream](https://github.com/NLnetLabs/unbound/blob/master/contrib/unbound.service.in), but not by [Debian](https://salsa.debian.org/dns-team/unbound/-/blob/master/debian/unbound.service). The `chroot` could also be enabled OOTB, like done upstream, and it should be additionally possible to run the service itself as `unbound` user, instead of relying on Unbound dropping privileges, adding port 53 permissions via privileges instead.
- It does not include the `resolvconf` handling done by the Debian package, which IMO causes more issues than it solves.
- It does not include the helper script from the Debian package, which does 3 things:
  1. Providing functions for the Debian-only `unbound-resolvconf.service`, which we do not ship as of above.
  2. Copy root trust anchor from `dns-root-data` package in place, which we skip, letting Unbound prime it from builtin data instead, if missing on first start. Unbound keeps these updated automatically, so it is relevant only on very first start. The only situation it could break is if the system stays offline for a very long time, so that both contained keys become invalid, making it impossible for Unbound to use them as basis for key updates. However, this really happens only every several years, and probably Unbound is then able (after upgrading the package) to replace the outdated keys with builtin ones, like if the file was missing. In any case simply removing the anchor file and upgrading the Unbound package (for up-to-date builtin keys) would solve it.
  3. Setting up a `chroot` if configured, which is not enabled by default with the Debian package. If it is wanted, we would set it up via systemd unit `BindPaths` instead.
- It ships without init.d service. Somehow, when upgrading the package, all config files of the old package, including `/etc/init.d/unbound` are appended to the `unbound.list` (static files) of the new package, and hence preserved until probably/hopefully only next package upgrade. I do not know the reason behind it. However, this means that additional processing is done when enabling/disabling the service after the upgrade, including two additional `systemd system-reload` steps etc, and the old service depends on the helper script, which is not available anymore. Hence our package manually removes that init.d service via `postinst` script.
- <s>It ships without Debian's `/etc/unbound/unbound.conf.d/remote-control.conf`, hence remote control needs to be enabled manually if needed, i.e. if `unbound-control` is used. Though, since it does not use a TCP port, but a UNIX socket, it is probably worth it to keep that one?</s> EDIT: Added as of user request.
_`/etc/unbound/unbound.conf.d/root-auto-trust-anchor-file.conf` for DNSSEC is included, of course._

I am happy to add sandboxing via systemd unit and/or `chroot` by default, the way the [upstream systemd unit](https://github.com/NLnetLabs/unbound/blob/master/contrib/unbound.service.in) does, and hence thankful for everyone who can help testing those directives.

### To test
Not necessarily needed, but at best update to DietPi v9.15. Then:
```sh
cd /tmp
wget "https://dietpi.com/downloads/binaries/$G_DISTRO_NAME/unbound_$G_HW_ARCH_NAME.deb"
apt install ./"unbound_$G_HW_ARCH_NAME.deb"
```

### There are some other changes, unrelated to the own builds:
- There is not much point to download root hints and update them via cron job. We could use the `dns-root-data` package, which ships and keeps them updated. However, root servers change only every several years, last update was one server ~3 years ago, And Unbound itself keeps them updated in their embedded list as well. For simplicity, since we aim to distribute our own package with ~instant updates on upstream release, and to align with upstream and Debian package defaults as well, we drop the external root hints usage entirely and rely on Unbound builtin data, getting also rid of one potential attack vector.
- Whenever we touch `/etc/unbound/unbound.conf.d/dietpi.conf`, potentially newly added settings (some just in case they were manually removed previously) are assured to be added within the `server:` block.
- The `unbound-resolvconf.service` is now not disabled _after_ package installation, but (in case disabled and) masked before the package installation, so it really never starts when installed via DietPi. Our own package won't ship it at all, it is a Debian-only maintainer implementation, not upstream, hence the mask is relevant for the Debian package, and in case someone decides to downgrade from our package to the original Debian package for some reason. In any case, we aim to be compatible with both for now.
